-117.79400,33.67570.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Ilene E. Hatch, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-0.18162,51.48431.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

144.95793,-37.80000.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by Peter Doherty Institute for Infection and Immunity. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 90 SqM. Operational or announced: 2014. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-71.13700,42.38990.name: Addgene
-71.13700,42.38990.desc: A non-profit repository through which laboratories deposit and share plasmids — the rings of DNA that carry an engineered construct. It has distributed well over a million, and it is the reason a technique published in a paper can be reproduced by someone else rather than remaining a claim. It is also a gate: shipping requires a verified institutional account, so the method is free to read and the material is not. It employs legal staff who negotiate a material transfer agreement with each depositing institution's technology transfer office, and standardised that step with electronic signatures on a universal agreement. That is what turned sharing engineered constructs from a bilateral negotiation into a catalogue order.

-0.12400,51.50000.name: Research ethics committees — lay membership and correspondence
-0.12400,51.50000.desc: Every clinical trial must be approved by an ethics committee, and those committees are required to include lay members — people from outside medicine and science, appointed as members of the public. Vacancies are advertised and the role is open to anyone. A committee will also accept correspondence about a study it approved. It is the only body in the medical half of this map with a seat reserved for someone with no professional interest in the answer.
